2609.09085.title: It's Not RoPE that Creates Sinks: The Role of Self-Concentration and Value-Non-Mixing in Attention
2609.09085.paper_summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) often exhibit "Attention Sink" (AS) and the accompanying "Massive Activations" (MAs) at the initial position of a sequence. These phenomena frequently co-occur, and MAs can pose challenges for low-bit quantization. In this study, we analyze the factors underlying AS and MAs that emerge at the initial position regardless of the token occupying it. Our experiments suggest that self-concentration of attention, resulting from the causal mask, and the subsequent Value-non-mixing in attention outputs contribute to AS and MAs. These findings provide new empirical evidence on the internal dynamics of LLMs, offering insights that may inform future quantization strategies and advance our understanding of the internal mechanisms of attention layers.
2609.09085.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）在序列的初始位置經常表現出「注意力沉沒」（AS）及隨之而來的「大規模激活」（MAs）。這些現象經常同時發生，而MAs可能對低位元量化造成挑戰。在本研究中，我們分析了無論佔據該位置的標記為何，出現在初始位置的AS和MAs背後的因素。我們的實驗表明，由因果遮罩導致的注意力自我集中，以及隨後在注意力輸出中出現的值非混合，對AS和MAs有所貢獻。這些發現為LLMs的內部動態提供了新的實證證據，並提供了可能有助於未來量化策略的見解，進一步加深我們對注意力層內部機制的理解。
2609.09085.author: Raito Kiya et.al.
